title: V114 versus Prevnar 13: the four solicited injection-site symptoms
question: In participants randomised to the 15-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine V114 or to the 13-valent comparator Prevnar 13, how does the risk of each solicited injection-site symptom compare?
_prose_rule: Every text field is PROSE unless it is on the numeric-text allowlist. Prose may not contain a bare numeral: any number it needs is a braced reference resolved at build time.
_sourcing_rule: Every MEASURED input names the source layer it came from. Values DERIVED by this build carry no source layer because they have no source: they are computed here and the validator recomputes them.

injection_site_pain.poolable_reason: NOT ONE OF THE SEVEN TRIALS REGISTERS THIS SYMPTOM AS AN OUTCOME MEASURE. Each registers a SINGLE solicited injection-site endpoint -- 'Percentage of Participants With a Solicited Injection-site Adverse Event' or its close variant -- and the individual symptoms appear only as CLASSES inside that measure's posted results. So the quantity is registry-sourced and real, but the four outcomes this page separates were never separated by the trials: they are components of one registered composite, reported alongside each other and never pre-specified as endpoints in their own right. A synthesis of them carries no pre-specification and cannot be protected against selective reporting by the registrations, because the registrations do not name them. SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON -- THE OBSERVATION WINDOWS DO NOT MATCH: two trials solicit over FIVE days and five over FOURTEEN. A fourteen-day window will record symptoms a five-day window cannot, so the same symptom is not the same measurement across these trials. Registered windows, verbatim: Up to 14 days after vaccination (NCT02547649); Up to 5 days after Vaccination 1 (NCT03547167); Up to Day 5 postvaccination (NCT03950622); Up to ~14 days after each vaccination (NCT03620162); Up to Day 14 after each study vaccination (NCT03692871); Day 1 to Day 14 post each vaccination (NCT03848065); Through 14 Days after Vaccination 1 (NCT03921424). No estimate was ever displayed for these outcomes and none is created here; this records WHY the object's existing poolable=False is correct, which it previously asserted with no reason recorded.

authority.handbook: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions
authority.sections: 8.7 (it is risk of bias); 3.1, 3.2.4.1 and MECIR 3.2.d (it is NOT eligibility); chapter 13 (exclusion is not required); 10.14 (sensitivity analysis)
authority.question: A contributing trial's registration does not declare the endpoint this synthesis takes from it. Is that an ELIGIBILITY question or a RISK OF BIAS question, and must the result be excluded from the primary synthesis?
authority.answer: RISK OF BIAS, not eligibility. The result STAYS in the primary synthesis, the trial is graded at high risk of bias in the domain covering selection of the reported result, and any analysis excluding it is reported as a SENSITIVITY analysis.

it_is_a_risk_of_bias_question.what: RoB 2 domain 5, 'bias in selection of the reported result'.
it_is_a_risk_of_bias_question.verbatim_scope: Covers bias arising when 'the reported result is selected (based on its direction, magnitude or statistical significance) from among multiple intervention effect estimates that were calculated by the trial authors'.
it_is_a_risk_of_bias_question.verbatim_method: 'attempt to retrieve the pre-specified analysis intentions for each trial ... allows for the identification of any outcome measures or analyses that have been omitted from, or added to, the results report, post hoc'.
it_is_a_risk_of_bias_question.why_it_fits: An outcome ADDED post hoc is precisely what this domain exists to grade. Our three instances are all of that kind -- the quantity exists in the publication and not in the registration.

it_is_NOT_an_eligibility_question.verbatim_3_1: 'Outcomes usually are not part of the criteria for including studies, and a Cochrane review would typically seek all sufficiently rigorous studies (most commonly randomized trials) of a particular comparison of interventions in a particular population of participants, irrespective of the outcomes measured or reported.'
it_is_NOT_an_eligibility_question.verbatim_3_2_4_1: 'Reporting of outcomes should rarely determine study eligibility for a review. In particular, studies should not be excluded because they do not report results of an outcome they may have measured, or provide "no usable data".'
it_is_NOT_an_eligibility_question.verbatim_mecir_3_2_d: 'Outcome measures should not always form part of the criteria for including studies in a review.'
it_is_NOT_an_eligibility_question.so: The Handbook does not merely permit inclusion -- it DISCOURAGES using outcome reporting as an eligibility criterion at all. Eligibility rests on the PICO elements and study design. Registration status is not among them.

the_handbook_does_not_require_exclusion.chapter: 13 (bias due to missing results in a synthesis)
the_handbook_does_not_require_exclusion.finding: Chapter 13 nowhere recommends excluding a non-pre-specified result from the primary synthesis. Its recommended handling is DETECTION (13.3.1.3, comparing study plans against available results), a RISK OF BIAS JUDGEMENT using the ROB-ME tool (13.3.5), and SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (13.3.4.6) -- not exclusion.
the_handbook_does_not_require_exclusion.and_a_distinction_that_matters: Chapter 13 and ROB-ME address results MISSING from a synthesis. Our case is the opposite direction -- a result PRESENT that was never pre-specified -- which is why section 8.7 is the correct instrument and Chapter 13 is the adjacent one. Section 8.7 says so itself: it 'does not address bias due to selective non-reporting (or incomplete reporting) of outcome domains that were measured and analysed by the trial authors'.

sensitivity_analysis_authority.verbatim: 'Sensitivity analyses should be used to examine whether overall findings are robust to potentially influential decisions.'

authority.the_conservative_principle: WHERE THE HANDBOOK LEAVES A CHOICE, TAKE THE OPTION THAT DOES NOT MOVE A RESULT TOWARD SIGNIFICANCE BY OUR OWN DECISION. An analytic choice of ours that STRENGTHENS our own conclusion needs a stronger justification than one that weakens it. Here the direction decides on its own: a wrong inclusion leaves a null intact, while a wrong exclusion publishes a positive result we created.
authority.how_this_was_verified: The ruling to adopt this reading came from the author. An author's agreement is not a source, so both propositions that would OVERTURN it were tested before it was applied: (1) does the Handbook place a non-pre-specified outcome under ELIGIBILITY? Chapter 3 says the opposite and discourages outcome-based exclusion. (2) is it explicit that such results should be EXCLUDED from primary synthesis? Chapter 13 recommends detection, a risk-of-bias judgement and sensitivity analysis instead. Both fail; the Handbook is more emphatic than the ruling.

injection_site_pain.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

not_poolable_reason_superseded_2026_08_1.was: These trials differ in observation window and in who records the symptom, so no estimate is combined across all of them.
not_poolable_reason_superseded_2026_08_1.why: IT CONTRADICTED THE OBJECT'S OWN poolable_reason AND IT WAS THE ONE THE PAGE RENDERED. The short field said the trials DIFFER IN WHO RECORDS the symptom; the long field says NO TRIAL REGISTERS IT AT ALL. Both cannot hold -- if nobody records it, there is no difference in who does. The builder prefers not_poolable_reason over poolable_reason, so the page carried the false claim and shadowed the true one. THIS WAS NEVER A REASON THAT FAILED TO REACH THE PAGE; a reason reached it and it was the wrong reason, which is why a presence check could not find it.

injection_site_pain.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is TRUE and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against PATISIRAN, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a DIFFERENT TRIAL. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In participants randomised to the 15-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine V114 or to the 13-valent comparator Prevnar 13, how does the risk of each solicited injection-site symptom compare?

It examines 7 randomised trials and DOES NOT POOL THEM.

The outcomes sought are Injection-site pain or tenderness; Injection-site swelling; Injection-site erythema or redness; Injection-site induration or hard lump.
